IS : 3400 ( Part XII ) 0 1971 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definition shall apply.

2.1 Tear Strength-The force required to cause a nick cut in a rubber test piece to extend by the tearing of the rubber, acting substantially parallel to the major axis or normal to the plane of the cut. 3. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD of cutting the force a slit of accurate depth in a special test required to tear across the width of the can at present test results and in this method observed.

3.1 The test consists piece and measuring uncut portion.

3.2 The choice of a method for determining tear strength be based only on considerations of reproducibility of the ease of carrying out the test; the crescent tear described will fulfil these requirements if the precautions specified are 4. IS : 3400 ( Part XII) - 1971 ' 4.1.1 The test piece shall be clamped firmly in a vertical plane, The cutting shall especially in the region where the nick is introduced. be done by means of a razor blade clamped in a vertical plane at right angles to the test piece. The blade holder or the clamped test piece shall be mounted on guide rails which ensures an exact horizontal motion without any lateral movement and also exact centering of the nick. The cutter shall be fitted with a micrometer gauge for controlling the depth of the nick: The blade shall be wetted with water or soap solution during nicking. 4.2 Micrometer Dial Gauge-The instrument tbr measuring the thickness of tear test pieces shall consist of a micrometer dial gauge firmly held in a rigid stand over a flat base plate of diameter at least 50 mm. The gauge shall have a scale graduated in unit divisions of 0.01 mm. The dial gauge shall be fitted with a flat contact, square to the plunger and parallel to the base plate, and shall operate with a pressure of 02 i QO3 kgf/cms ( 20 f 3KN/m2 ) .
NOTE -It is preferable for the gauge to have a contact area of diameter about 4 mm aa this may be used on almost all test pieces without any sub-part of the contact area overhanging the test piece edge, which would increase the contact pressure.

4.3 Meamuring Inmtrnment - For measuring the depth of the nick an optical instrument shall be used, the test piece being mounted so that the nick is slightly opened in order to make it visible. 4.3.1 When it is only necessary to check that the depth of the nick is within the specified limits, any suitable means may be used, for example, an optical projection apparatus. A convenient arrangement is a microscope giving about 100 x magnification and fitted with travelling stage suitably illuminated. The eyepiece is fitted with a graticule by which to record the travel of the stage and test piece through a distance equal to the depth of the nick. The travel of the stage is calibrated with a stage micrometer graticule. 4.3.2 Alternatively, a travelling microscope may be used. The apparatus &all allow an accuracrof measurement of at least 0.025 mm. 4.4 Tensile Testing Machine-The tensile testing machine shall be power driven and of such capacity that the maximum force required for the test is not greater than 85 percent nor less than 15 percent of the maximum of the scale. The rate of traverse of the driven grip shall be 500 f ,50 mm/min and the power shall be sufficient to maintain the rate substantially constant up to the maximum capacity of the machine. The machine shall be equipped to give a continuous indication of the force on the test piece during the uninterrupted stretching of the test piece. After the test piece has broken, the indicators shall remain at the point of maximum force. The machine shall be provided with a type of grip which tightens 5

IS : 3400 ( Part XII ) - 1971 automatically as the tension increases and exerts a Each grip across the widened end of the test piece. positioning device so that all test pieces are inserted to 20 mm and are in axial alignment with the direction of uniform pressure shall incorporate a a depth of 15 to pull.

NOTE--- The force scale shall be calibrated by a suitable method at least every six months to ensure that the errror does not exceed 1'5 percent of the applied force or O-3 percent of the maximum of the scale whichever is greater.

test piece shall be between 1.8 to 2.8 mm, and shall be measured by means of microThe thickness in the region of the test area than 2 percent from the mean.

5.1.2 A single nick or slit of O-50 f 0.08 mm depth shall be cut with extreme care and accuracy, symmetrically across the centre of the concave The variation between the nick depth on inner edge of the test piece. either side of the test piece shall not be more than 10 percent. Test pieces falling out of the tolerance specified for the nick shall be discarded. 6. TEMPERATURE OF TEST

6.1 Carry ant the test at 27 i 2�C unless otherwise specified. Some synthetic rubbers have markedly lower tear strength at elevated temperatures and hence tests may also have to be carried out at higher tempers ture, 100�C being the useful temperature. 7. PROCEDURE 7,l l'est at least, three, but preferably six, test pieces.

or embodied 7.2 Preparation of the Sample - If a fabric is attached in the rubber sample, remove the same before cutting the test pieces. Avoid preferably the use of a swelling agent while removing the fabric, but benzene; chloroform or carbon tetrachloride may be used to wet the Take care to avoid stretching of the contacting surfaces, if necessary. rubber durin the separation from the fabric, and if swelling liquid is used, allow t a e same to evaporate completely from the rubber surfaces 6

after scparat ion. Make the cloth marked surfxes smooth by buffing. Buff as and when necessary the rubber sample of uneven thickness, or of thickness above the maxim!Im specified for the test piece which is to be cut from it. During l&ling avoid undue heating of the rubber. 7.3 Conditioning of Test PiecesThe properties of vulcanized rubbers change continuollsly with time, these changes being particularly rapid Do not carry out any test during the first 24 `hours: after vulcanization. during this period; for accurate comparison between different rubbers it may be necessary to ensure that these are tested at substantially the Protect test pieces as far as possible same interval after ~ulcani~;~lion. from light. Condition samples after any necessary preparation at the test temperature for not less than 16 hours immediately before testing. 7.4 Nicking the Test Piece-Nick the test piece during period, preferably tobvards the end of the period. 7.5 Measurement of Test Pieces -Four the region of the test arc shall be made used in the formula given in 8. the conditioning

NOTEThe depth of tile nick on both sides of the test piece shall be measured Any test piece in which the depth of the nick on and the average value calculated. either side is outside the limits stated above shall he discarded. The effective width of the test piece shall be taken as the mmimum width of the die ( IO.5 mm) minus the average depth of the nick.

7.6 Determination of Tear Strength-Insert the test piece in the grips of the tensile testing machine, taking care to adjust it symmetrically so that tearing shall proceed in a plane normal to the direction of pull. Note Then start the machine and do not stop until the test piece breaks. the maximum load reached during the tearing along with the average thickness of the specimen. 8. CALCULATION
8.1 The tear strength depends upon the width and thickness of the test piece and the result is expressed as the force (in kilogram force) necessary to tear a test piece of standard width and thickness.
